samples.summary: Second copy of `mayHaveUnsent` was not revisited when `SyncState` gained `saved-locally`
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/use-unsaved-work-probe.ts:24` still reads `const mayHaveUnsent = state === 'not-saved' || state === 'saving';`. The diff changed `deriveSyncState` so that a durable document with unsent work now reports `'saved-locally'` instead of `'not-saved'`, and it updated the chip's own copy of this predicate (`sync-status-chip.tsx`, which grew `leavingLosesWork = mayHaveUnsent || savedLocally`). This out-of-diff copy was left alone, so on a durable document the probe no longer registers with `lib/unsaved-work.ts` and `lazy-with-retry.ts:158`/`:233` will now take the recovery `env.reload()` it previously refused. A full-page reload is arguably safe for a durable entry (that is the point of the state), so this may well be the intended answer — but nothing in the code or in `docs/design/sync-status.md:246` records the divergence, and the chip's own reasoning that *closing* the document removes the entry does not obviously carry over. Worth an explicit decision plus a comment, since the two predicates now differ silently.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` now issues two extra requests (including an unfiltered `GET /documents`) on every call, unguarded
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:127` calls `documentIdsIn(id)` unconditionally before the DELETE, and `documentIdsIn` (`workspaces.ts:101-115`) performs `fetchWorkspace(ref)` plus a full unfiltered `fetchDocuments()`. `removeMember` guards the identical work behind `isOfflineUser(...)` at `workspaces.ts:159-160`, but `deleteWorkspace` has no equivalent gate, so the out-of-diff caller `packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:182` (`mutationFn: () => deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)`) now pays two extra round-trips — one of them a listing of every document the user can read — before every workspace deletion, even on the shipped pin where `@yorkie-js/react` is `0.7.22` (`packages/frontend/package.json:66`) and `purgeOfflineDocuments` is guaranteed to be a no-op. Cheapest fix: gate `documentIdsIn` on the same condition the purge already checks.

samples.summary: `api/auth.ts` now statically pulls the whole offline stack (and a module-scope `storage` listener) into every public entry point
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:4` adds `import { eraseOfflineDataOnLogout } from "@/lib/offline-erase"`, and `offline-erase.ts` value-imports `WafflebaseDocStore`, `durable-session.ts` and `offline-persistence-preference.ts`. `@/api/auth` is imported by unauthenticated entry points that previously touched none of this — `packages/frontend/src/app/home/marketing-page.tsx:2`, `packages/frontend/src/app/home-or-redirect.tsx:2`, `packages/frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx:4`, `packages/frontend/src/app/templates/template-landing.tsx:29`. As a side effect, `offline-persistence-preference.ts` registers a module-scope `window.addEventListener('storage', ...)` on the landing and login pages. Chunk-size budgets are an enforced lane and will speak for themselves; the unconditional module-scope listener on anonymous pages is the part nothing checks. A dynamic `import()` inside `logout()` would keep the erase off those entry points.

samples.summary: API table still describes `deleteDocument`/`deleteDocuments` as plain HTTP wrappers
samples.evidence: `docs/design/frontend.md:478-479` maps `deleteDocument(id)` → `DELETE /documents/:id` and `deleteDocuments(ids)` → `POST /documents/delete`. Both now additionally perform local IndexedDB cleanup via `purgeOfflineDocuments` (`packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:167` and `:215`), which is a side effect a reader of this table would not expect. The backticked-path lane checks that paths resolve, not that descriptions are current, so nothing catches this.
